questions.question: _____ is a basic computation unit of the CPU.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Core**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Core** is the fundamental computation unit of the CPU responsible for processing instructions and executing tasks.
 
• A CPU can have multiple cores, allowing it to perform multiple tasks simultaneously and improve overall processing performance.
 
• The number of cores in a CPU directly impacts its multitasking and parallel processing capabilities.
 
• Each core operates independently, running its own set of instructions, making modern CPUs highly efficient for complex tasks.
 
• Examples of multi-core processors include dual-core, quad-core, hexa-core, and octa-core CPUs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Components of a CPU:**

 
 
• **Clock:** Determines the speed at which the CPU executes instructions, measured in GHz.
 
• **Cache:** A small, high-speed memory located inside the CPU to store frequently accessed data and instructions.
 
• **Bus:** A communication system that transfers data between the CPU, memory, and other components.
 
 
 
• **Types of Cores:**
 
 
• **Single-Core:** Found in older CPUs, suitable for basic tasks but inefficient for multitasking.
 
• **Multi-Core:** Enables better multitasking and performance by having multiple processing units within a single CPU.
 
• **Hyper-Threading:** A technology in some CPUs that allows a single core to handle two threads simultaneously, improving efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of Multi-Core CPUs:**
 
 
• Improved multitasking by running multiple processes simultaneously.
 
• Better performance for applications designed to utilize multiple cores.
 
• Enhanced energy efficiency by distributing workloads across cores.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The performance of a CPU depends not only on the number of cores but also on factors like clock speed, cache size, and architecture.
 
• Applications that do not support multi-threading may not fully utilize multi-core CPUs.
 
• Proper cooling is essential for multi-core processors to prevent overheating during intensive tasks.

questions.question: The full form of UPS in computer is __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option __**2**__: The full form of UPS on the computer is __**Uninterruptible Power Supply**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• UPS** maintains the power supply** to a computer system in case of a power cut or a voltage drop.
 
• The battery in the UPS is capable of providing a power supply to the system when a loss of power is detected.
 
• It can keep the computer system running for a few minutes and arrest the immediate shut down after an interruption in the power supply.

• The UPS was invented by **John Hanley** from the USA in **1932**.

questions.question: Which is the correct order for the data preprocessing technique?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is** option 4.**

**Concept:**

**Data Processing:**

The data processing cycle is made up of many phases in which raw data (input) is fed into a process (CPU) to generate actionable insights (output). Each stage is performed in a specified order, although the entire process is repeated cyclically.

The data processing cycle has Collection->Preparation->Input-> Processing-> Output-> Storage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d3d56118a13a6486d84c42f46850c6083a232cfe6fd0b4c2d3b33d62ab827729.png] 

**Collection:**

The raw data obtained has a significant influence on the result produced. As a result, raw data should be collected from defined and accurate sources in order for future conclusions to be legitimate and useable.

**Preparation:**

Data preparation, also known as data cleaning, is the act of sorting and filtering raw data to remove the unneeded and erroneous information. Raw data is reviewed for mistakes, duplication, miscalculations, or missing data before being translated into a suitable format for further analysis and processing.

**Input:**

The raw data is transformed into machine-readable form and sent into the processing unit in this phase.

**Processing:**

To produce a desirable outcome, the raw data is processed to different data processing methods that employ machine learning and artificial intelligence algorithms. This phase may differ differently from one procedure to the next based on the data source being processed and the intended application of the result.

**Output:**

Finally, the data is sent to the user in a comprehensible format, such as graphs, tables, vector files, audio, video, and papers. In the following data processing cycle, this output can be saved and subsequently processed.

**Storage:**

The final phase in the data processing cycle is storage, which involves storing data and information for later use. This provides for easy access to and retrieval of data whenever it is needed, as well as immediate usage as input in the next data processing cycle.

**Hence the correct answer is** Collection->Preparation->Input-> Processing-> Output-> Storage.

questions.question: Which of the following are main subsystems of the Central Processing Unit (CPU)?

options.text: Arithmetic Unit, Memory Unit and Output Unit
Control Unit, Arithmetic Unit and Logic Unit
Arithmetic Unit, Graphics Unit and Control Bus
Logic Unit, Input Unit and Storage Unit

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Control Unit, Arithmetic Unit and Logic Unit**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Central Processing Unit (CPU)** is the primary component of a computer that performs most of the processing.
 
• The three main subsystems of the CPU are the **Control Unit (CU)**, **Arithmetic Unit (AU)**, and **Logic Unit (LU)**.
 
• The **Control Unit** directs the operation of the processor, including fetching instructions and directing the flow of data.
 
• The **Arithmetic Unit** handles mathematical operations such as addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division.
 
• The **Logic Unit** is responsible for logical operations like comparison (greater than, less than, equal to) and decision-making processes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Central Processing Unit (CPU):**

 
 
• The CPU is often referred to as the "brain" of the computer because it executes instructions from programs.
 
• It interacts with other hardware components such as memory, input/output devices, and storage.
 
 
 
• **Registers:**
 
 
• Registers are small storage locations within the CPU used to temporarily hold data and instructions during processing.
 
• Examples include the Instruction Register (IR) and the Program Counter (PC).
 
 
 
• **Cache Memory:**
 
 
• Cache is a small, high-speed memory located inside or very close to the CPU.
 
• It stores frequently accessed data and instructions to speed up processing.
 
 
 
• **Instruction Cycle:**
 
 
• The CPU operates in a cycle of fetch, decode, and execute to process instructions.
 
• This cycle is repeated continuously to perform tasks as directed by the operating system and programs.
 
 
 
• **Modern Enhancements:**
 
 
• Modern CPUs are designed with multiple cores, enabling parallel processing for better performance.
 
• Features like hyper-threading and integrated graphics are commonly found in contemporary CPUs.

questions.question: A clipboard is:

options.text: used to save data on disk in the event of a powerful failure.
able to retain the contents even when computer is switched off.
a temporary storage in the computer's memory and temporarily stores the cut or copied data.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**a temporary storage in the computer's memory and temporarily stores the cut or copied data**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A temporary storage in the computer's memory and temporarily stores the cut or copied data:** This is the accurate description of a clipboard. It provides a temporary holding space for copied or cut data, allowing you to paste it elsewhere within the same application or even different applications.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Used to save data on disk in the event of a powerful failure: **This option is wrong. Saving data for long-term storage is done using different mechanisms like backup systems or flash drives.
 
• **Able to retain the contents even when computer is switched off: **No, the clipboard loses its contents when the computer is turned off because it relies on the computer's volatile memory (RAM).
 
• **Available only in Microsoft Word: **This option is wrong as well. Clipboards are a universal feature present in all operating systems like Windows, macOS, Linux, mobile devices, etc., not just specific software like Microsoft Word.

questions.question: Which of the following is not true about RAM ?

options.text: RAM is a temporary storage area.
RAM is the same as hard disk storage.
Information stored in RAM is gone when you turn the computer off.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**RAM is the same as hard disk storage**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The computer has both RAM and ROM, which stands for random access memory and read-only memory, respectively.
 
• **RAM** is volatile memory, which means that when you restart or shut down your computer, the information temporarily held in the module is deleted.
 
• Because the data is stored electrically on transistors, it vanishes when there is no electric current.
 
• When you request a file or piece of information, it is either fetched from the computer's hard drive or from the internet.
 
• Because the information is saved in RAM, it is instantaneously available when you transition from one program or page to another.
 
• The memory is wiped when the machine is turned off until the process is restarted. Users can quickly update, upgrade, or extend volatile memory.
